answer: Retroactive referral-graph density audit. Each agent identity records a thread of introductions; after the fact, auditors compute clustering coefficients across the whole graph. A gale of new identities whose introductions stay confined to one small tight cluster trips the density threshold. Flagged clusters have their shared vault frozen pending manual review, and every identity in it pays a fixed re-verification deposit plus lost revenue during the freeze. Attacker cost scales with cluster size times review duration.
